name: Bali
summary: Resort beaches in Nusa Dua, cliff temples in Uluwatu, Nusa Penida's coastline, Ubud's rice terraces and volcano sunrises, then Canggu sunsets.

months.note: Wet season. Busy over New Year, quiet after.
Wettest stretch and lowest prices. Short, heavy afternoon storms.
Nyepi (Day of Silence) usually falls in March: the whole island shuts for 24 hours, airport included. Check the date.
Dry season begins. Green rice terraces, fair prices.
Dry, green and not yet crowded.
Dry. School holidays push prices up from late June.
Peak season: driest, busiest, priciest. Book stays early.
Peak season continues. Best weather for Nusa Penida boats and Mount Batur.
Still dry with fewer crowds. A sweet spot.
Warm and calm before the rains.
Wet, and very busy from Christmas to New Year.

tips.title: Visa on arrival
tips.body: Most nationalities need a visa. Buy the e-VOA online before you fly: IDR 500,000 (about US$31), valid 30 days and extendable once for 30 more. Your passport needs at least 6 months left.

tips.title: All Indonesia arrival card
tips.body: Fill in the free All Indonesia form online within 3 days before landing. It covers immigration, customs and health in one QR code you show at the airport.

tips.title: Bali tourist levy
tips.body: Every foreign visitor pays IDR 150,000 (about US$10) once per trip. Pay on the official Love Bali site or app before you fly and keep the receipt QR code.

tips.title: Cash and ATMs
tips.body: The currency is the rupiah (IDR). Use ATMs inside banks or malls and authorised money changers. Skip street changers offering better-than-market rates: short-changing is common.

tips.title: Tipping
tips.body: Not expected. Many restaurants already add about 15% for service and tax. Round up for drivers, and leave IDR 20,000–50,000 for a good spa therapist or guide.

tips.title: Plugs and power
tips.body: Type C and F sockets (two round pins), 230 V. Bring a universal adapter.

tips.title: Temple dress
tips.body: Cover shoulders and knees and wear a sarong and sash. Most temples lend or rent them at the gate. Don't step on the small offerings (canang) on the ground.

tips.title: Bali belly
tips.body: Drink bottled or filtered water only, also for brushing teeth. Pack rehydration salts just in case.

tips.title: Rabies and monkeys
tips.body: Bali has rabies. Don't touch monkeys or stray dogs, and keep food, glasses and phones out of reach at Uluwatu and the Monkey Forest. If bitten or scratched, see a clinic the same day.

tips.title: Mosquitoes
tips.body: Dengue occurs year-round, more in the wet season. Use repellent with DEET or picaridin, especially at dawn and dusk.

tips.title: Taxis and scooters
tips.body: Grab and Gojek apps are the easiest way to get cars and scooter taxis; some areas only allow local drivers. Renting a scooter needs an International Driving Permit that covers motorbikes, or insurance may not pay.

tips.title: Ocean and cliffs
tips.body: Currents are strong on many beaches: swim between the red-and-yellow flags. On Nusa Penida, stay well back from the edges at Angel's Billabong and Devil's Tear.

tips.title: Travel insurance
tips.body: Get cover that includes medical evacuation, and scooter accidents if you plan to ride.

places.name: Marriott's Bali Nusa Dua Gardens
places.blurb: Resort hotel in Bali's gated Nusa Dua enclave, a short shuttle from the beach. Bookable with Marriott points, which is why points travellers start their trip here.

places.name: Nusa Dua Beach
places.blurb: Calm, white-sand resort beach on the sheltered east side of the Bukit, with a paved promenade.

places.name: Geger Beach
places.blurb: Quiet local favourite at the south end of Nusa Dua, with seaweed farms at low tide.

places.name: Pandawa Beach
places.blurb: White-sand beach below carved limestone cliffs, reached by a road cut through the rock.

places.name: Bali Collection
places.blurb: Open-air shopping and dining complex inside the Nusa Dua resort enclave. Handy for essentials and a stroll rather than a destination in itself.

places.name: Uluwatu Temple
places.blurb: Thousand-year-old sea temple perched on a 70 m cliff edge at Bali's southwestern tip. One of the island's six holiest temples, famous for sunsets and bold macaques.

places.name: Kecak Dance Performance
places.blurb: Traditional fire dance performed at sunset in Uluwatu Temple's clifftop amphitheatre, with a chanting choir of dozens of men instead of instruments. Telling of the Ramayana epic.

places.name: Bumbu Bali
places.blurb: Long-running Balinese fine-dining restaurant by chef Heinz von Holzen, known for its rijsttafel set menu and cooking school. A classic for authentic Balinese food.

places.name: Ferry from Sanur to Nusa Penida
places.blurb: Fast boats cross from Sanur to Nusa Penida in about 45 minutes. Book a morning boat; the strait gets choppy in the afternoon.

places.name: West Nusa Penida (Kelingking Beach, Angel's Billabong, Broken Beach, Crystal Bay)
places.blurb: Day-tour circuit of Nusa Penida's west coast: the T-rex-shaped Kelingking cliff, Angel's Billabong rock pool, Broken Beach's natural arch and Crystal Bay for snorkelling.

places.name: Diamond Beach
places.blurb: White-sand cove on Nusa Penida's east coast, reached by a cliff-carved staircase, with palm trees and diamond-shaped rock pinnacles in the surf.

places.name: Maruti Beach Club
places.blurb: Laid-back beach club on Nusa Penida where a sunbed comes with a minimum food-and-drink spend. A rest stop between the island's viewpoints.

places.name: Sanur to Ubud Drive
places.blurb: Private car from the coast up to Ubud, about 90 minutes depending on traffic. Drivers usually stop at sights on request.

places.name: Ubud Art Market
places.blurb: Traditional market opposite Ubud's royal palace selling woven bags, sarongs, carvings and art. Free to wander; bargaining is expected.

places.name: Mount Batur Sunrise Hike
places.blurb: Pre-dawn hike up a 1,717 m active volcano for sunrise above a sea of clouds and the caldera lake. About two hours up on a well-trodden path with a guide.

places.name: Tegalalang Rice Terraces
places.blurb: Bali's most photographed rice terraces, carved into a river valley north of Ubud using the island's thousand-year-old subak irrigation system.

places.name: Goa Gajah & Pura Gunung Lebah
places.blurb: Goa Gajah, the 9th-century 'Elephant Cave' sanctuary with its carved demon-mouth entrance, paired with the small river-junction temple Pura Gunung Lebah in Ubud.

places.name: Copper Kitchen and Bar
places.blurb: Rooftop restaurant at Bisma Eight in Ubud doing modern plates with local produce. A dressier dinner option without resort prices.

places.name: Alchemy
places.blurb: Raw-vegan cafe in Penestanan, known for its build-your-own salad and breakfast bar.

places.name: Umah Pizza
places.blurb: Small wood-fired pizza place on Jalan Bisma.

places.name: Warung de Koi
places.blurb: Local warung on the road to Tirta Empul temple, about 15 km north-east of Ubud.

places.name: No Más
places.blurb: Loud, late cocktail bar just off Jalan Monkey Forest.

places.name: CP Lounge
places.blurb: Late-night bar and club on Jalan Monkey Forest with live music, open until 3am.

places.name: Radiantly Alive
places.blurb: Big open-air yoga studio on Jalan Jembawan in central Ubud, with drop-in classes from beginner flows to aerial.

places.name: Ubud Yoga House
places.blurb: Small studio in the rice fields of Subak Sokwayah, a 10-minute walk from Jalan Raya.

places.name: Pura Tanah Lot
places.blurb: 16th-century temple on a rock just offshore, cut off at high tide. One of Bali's most sacred sea temples and its most famous sunset silhouette.

places.name: Canggu Beach Clubs (The Lawn, Finns, La Brisa)
places.blurb: Canggu's beachfront clubs: grassy sunset drinks at The Lawn, pool parties at Finns, and driftwood-chic La Brisa. Entry is free; daybeds carry a minimum spend.

places.name: The Shady Shack
places.blurb: Breezy vegetarian cafe by Canggu's rice fields that became one of Bali's best-known healthy-food spots. Expect smoothie bowls and big veggie burgers.

places.name: Coffee Cartel
places.blurb: Instagram-famous Seminyak brunch cafe known for latte art, pastel interiors and health-leaning breakfast plates.

places.name: Prana Spa
places.blurb: Moroccan-Rajasthani styled spa in Seminyak, one of Bali's most elaborate day spas, doing massages, rituals and hammam treatments.

places.name: W Hotel
places.blurb: Flashy beachfront resort on Seminyak's sand, known for its pool scene and Woobar sunsets. The splurge stay of this route.

places.name: Merah Putih
places.blurb: Striking high-ceilinged restaurant serving modern Indonesian food; the 10-dish tasting menu tours the archipelago's cuisines.

places.name: The Edge
places.blurb: Clifftop resort above Uluwatu whose day pass buys access to the famous glass-edged 'oneeighty' pool hanging over the ocean, with food-and-drink credit included.

places.name: Green Bowl Beach
places.blurb: Secluded white-sand beach at the bottom of about 300 steps on the Bukit's south coast, shared with surfers and bats in its cliff caves.

places.name: Sundays Beach Club
places.blurb: Beach club on a private white-sand cove below the cliffs at Ungasan, reached by inclinator. Day pass includes food-and-drink credit, kayaks and snorkelling.

places.name: Sarong
places.blurb: Elegant Seminyak dining room by chef Will Meyrick doing refined South-East Asian street food. A long-standing special-occasion pick.
places.tip: Closed: Sarong's own site says it will reopen next year in a new location.

places.name: Ubud Shopping
places.blurb: Boutique-hopping along Ubud's Jalan Dewi Sita and Hanoman streets: homeware, jewellery and clothes beyond the market stalls.

places.name: Ubud Palace evening dance
places.blurb: Evening Legong and Barong dance performances in the courtyard of Puri Saren Agung, Ubud's royal palace, still home to the town's royal family.

places.name: Tirta Gangga Water Palace
places.blurb: Former royal water palace in East Bali from 1946, with koi-filled pools, fountains and stepping stones, built around a spring the Balinese hold sacred.

places.name: Gates of Heaven (Lempuyang Temple)
places.blurb: Lempuyang Temple's famous split gate framing Mount Agung. The 'reflection' in photos is a trick done with a mirror under a phone, and queues run for hours.

places.name: Ubud Rafting
places.blurb: White-water rafting on the Ayung River's class II-III rapids through jungle gorges and past waterfalls, with hotel pickup included on most tours.

places.name: Tegenungan Waterfall
places.blurb: Powerful 15 m waterfall near Ubud, one of Bali's most visited, with a swimmable pool and a staircase of viewpoints.

places.name: Tirta Empul Temple
places.blurb: Thousand-year-old water temple where Balinese Hindus queue through 13 fountain spouts for the melukat purification ritual. Visitors can join with a guide and a sarong.

places.name: Bajra Sandhi Monument
places.blurb: A large monument in Renon's Niti Mandala park honouring the Balinese struggle for independence, with a history museum of dioramas and a 360-degree viewing deck at the top.

places.name: Pasar Badung
places.blurb: Denpasar's biggest traditional market, beside the Badung River: several floors of produce, spices, temple offerings and textiles sold to locals.

places.name: Warung Blanjong
places.blurb: Family-run Sanur warung known for nasi campur and Balinese home cooking.

places.name: Sanur Beach
places.blurb: Calm, reef-protected beach on Bali's east coast with a long beachfront path. Known for sunrises and easy family swimming.

places.name: Puri Santrian
places.blurb: Long-running beachfront resort in Sanur with tropical gardens and several pools.

places.name: Single Fin
places.blurb: Clifftop bar and restaurant above the Uluwatu surf break, famous for sunset sessions and its Sunday night party.

places.name: Padang Padang Beach
places.blurb: Small cove reached through a narrow gap in the limestone cliffs, famous from Eat Pray Love and for its world-class reef break.

places.name: Jimbaran Bay seafood dinner
places.blurb: Rows of beach cafés on Jimbaran Bay grill the day's catch over coconut husks, served at tables on the sand at sunset.

places.name: InterContinental Bali Resort
places.blurb: Large beachfront resort on Jimbaran Bay, close to the seafood cafés.

places.name: Waterblow
places.blurb: Limestone outcrop where ocean swells smash into the rocks and shoot spray high into the air. Most dramatic at high tide.

places.name: KU DE TA
places.blurb: Seminyak's original beachfront club: daybeds, cocktails and sunset DJs on the sand.

places.name: Motel Mexicola
places.blurb: Loud, colourful Mexican cantina in Seminyak, as much party as restaurant.

places.name: Pura Petitenget
places.blurb: 16th-century sea temple linked to the priest Dang Hyang Nirartha, one of the chain of temples guarding Bali's southwest coast.

places.name: Hotel Tugu Bali
places.blurb: Boutique hotel on Batu Bolong beach filled with antique Indonesian art, built like a museum you can sleep in.

places.name: Batu Bolong & Echo Beach
places.blurb: Neighbouring black-sand surf beaches at the heart of Canggu: Batu Bolong for beginner waves, Echo Beach for sunset bars and bigger breaks.

places.name: Crate Café
places.blurb: Busy Canggu breakfast café serving big brunch plates and smoothie bowls out of shipping-crate style digs.

places.name: Jatiluwih Rice Terraces
places.blurb: Sweeping terraces on the slopes of Mount Batukaru, part of the UNESCO-listed Subak landscape, with walking trails through the fields.

places.name: Taman Ayun Temple
places.blurb: Moated royal temple of the Mengwi kingdom, built in 1634 and part of the UNESCO Subak listing, known for its tiered meru shrines.

places.name: Sang Giri Mountain Glamping Camp
places.blurb: Safari-style tents in the forest above the Jatiluwih rice terraces.

places.name: Ulun Danu Beratan Temple
places.blurb: 17th-century water temple to the lake goddess Dewi Danu whose shrines seem to float on Lake Beratan. It is on the IDR 50,000 note.

places.name: Handara Gate
places.blurb: Traditional Balinese split gate at the entrance to Handara golf resort, framed by misty mountains. One of Bali's most photographed spots.

places.name: Banyumala Twin Waterfalls
places.blurb: Twin cascades in jungle above Lake Buyan, reached by a short steep trail, with a pool you can swim in.

places.name: Sacred Monkey Forest Sanctuary
places.blurb: Forest sanctuary in central Ubud with more than 1,000 long-tailed macaques, three 14th-century temples and moss-covered carvings.
places.tip: Keep sunglasses and snacks out of sight: the monkeys grab them.

places.name: Ubud Palace
places.blurb: Puri Saren Agung, home of Ubud's royal family, with ornate gates and courtyards. Free to walk in by day.

places.name: Campuhan Ridge Walk
places.blurb: Paved 2 km ridge-top trail between two river valleys, lined with tall grass. Best at sunrise before the heat.

places.name: Bisma Eight
places.blurb: Design hotel on Jalan Bisma with a jungle-view infinity pool, a short walk from central Ubud.

places.name: The Yoga Barn
places.blurb: Ubud's best-known yoga centre, running many classes a day in open-air studios among the rice fields.

places.name: Kintamani area entrance fee
places.blurb: Fee collected at checkpoints on the roads into the Batur caldera.

places.name: Toya Devasya Hot Springs
places.blurb: Volcanic hot-spring pools on the shore of Lake Batur beneath Mount Batur. A classic soak after the sunrise hike.

places.name: Penglipuran Village
places.blurb: Traditional village of matching bamboo-roofed compounds along a car-free street, often called one of the cleanest villages in the world.

places.name: Tukad Cepung Waterfall
places.blurb: Waterfall hidden inside a narrow canyon cave, famous for morning light beams through the rock.

places.name: Sidemen Valley & Bukit Tegeh
places.blurb: Quiet valley of rice terraces under Mount Agung. Bukit Tegeh hill gives the best view over it.

places.name: Virgin Beach
places.blurb: White-sand cove with turquoise water near Candidasa, lined with simple warungs. One of east Bali's few white-sand beaches.

places.name: Jemeluk Bay
places.blurb: Sheltered Amed bay with coral right off the beach, plus underwater statues and an underwater postbox.

places.name: Japanese Shipwreck
places.blurb: Small WWII-era patrol boat wreck in 2-12 m of water off Banyuning, coral-covered and easy to snorkel from shore.

places.name: Warung Enak
places.blurb: Simple Amed warung for nasi goreng, grilled fish and other Indonesian staples.

places.name: USAT Liberty wreck
places.blurb: US Army cargo ship torpedoed in 1942 that now lies just off the beach at 5-30 m, one of the world's most accessible wreck dives.

places.name: Lovina dolphin tour
places.blurb: Sunrise trips in traditional outrigger boats to see wild spinner dolphins off Lovina's black-sand coast.

places.name: Banjar Hot Springs
places.blurb: Sulphur springs pouring from carved dragon spouts into three tiered pools in a tropical garden.

places.name: Brahmavihara-Arama
places.blurb: Bali's largest Buddhist monastery, on a hillside above Lovina, with a mini Borobudur stupa.

places.name: Gitgit Waterfall
places.blurb: 35-40 m waterfall in jungle just off the Singaraja to Bedugul road.

places.name: Munduk Moding Plantation
places.blurb: Eco resort on a coffee plantation in the Munduk highlands, known for its infinity pool above the clouds.

places.name: Menjangan Island
places.blurb: Uninhabited island in West Bali National Park with steep coral walls and clear water, among Bali's best snorkelling.

places.name: Biorock Pemuteran
places.blurb: One of the world's largest reef-restoration projects: coral grows on electrified steel frames right off Pemuteran beach.

places.name: Taman Sari Bali Resort & Spa
places.blurb: Beachfront bungalows in Pemuteran, close to the Biorock reef.

places.name: Drive back to Denpasar
places.blurb: One-way private car from northwest Bali to the airport, about 4-5 hours.

places.name: Kampung Cafe
places.blurb: Café overlooking the Tegalalang rice terraces.

places.name: Layana Warung
places.blurb: Vegetarian-friendly warung near Goa Gajah.

places.name: Saraswati Temple
places.blurb: Water temple to Saraswati, goddess of learning, fronted by a lotus pond. Evening dance shows are held here.

places.name: Prasaja by Arang
places.blurb: Restaurant on Jalan Raya Ubud cooking over charcoal.

places.name: Ubud Traditional Spa
places.blurb: Well-reviewed day spa in Kedewatan, west of central Ubud, for traditional Balinese massage.

places.name: Bali Swing
places.blurb: The original jungle swing park, with giant swings over the Ayung River valley.

places.name: Potato Head Beach Club
places.blurb: Landmark Seminyak beach club with a lawn and infinity pool facing the sunset.

places.name: Surf lesson in Canggu
places.blurb: Batu Bolong and Echo Beach have gentle sandy-bottom waves and dozens of surf schools on the beach.

places.name: MyWarung
places.blurb: Casual Canggu warung serving Indonesian and western dishes.

places.name: Waterbom Bali
places.blurb: Landscaped waterpark in Kuta with more than a dozen slides, regularly ranked among Asia's best.

places.name: Suluban Beach
places.blurb: Hidden beach reached through a gap in the cliffs below the Uluwatu surf break, with caves and sunset views.

places.name: Warung Bejana
places.blurb: Restaurant about 400 m from Uluwatu Temple, handy before or after the Kecak show.

places.name: Tribal Bali
places.blurb: Co-working hostel with a big pool, popular with digital nomads.

places.name: Pura Besakih
places.blurb: Bali's Mother Temple: more than 80 temples on the slopes of Mount Agung, the holiest site in Balinese Hinduism.
places.tip: Go with a guide or tour: touts at the gate are known for scams.

places.name: Batur Natural Hot Spring
places.blurb: Hot-spring pools on the shore of Lake Batur with views of the volcano.

places.name: La Plancha
places.blurb: Beach bar known for colourful umbrellas and beanbags on the sand at sunset.

places.name: Airport taxi
places.blurb: Taxi between Ngurah Rai airport and your hotel.

places.name: Amar Boutique Hotel
places.blurb: Small boutique hotel in Pererenan, near Echo Beach.

places.name: The Kayon Jungle Resort
places.blurb: Adults-only jungle resort north of Ubud with tiered infinity pools over the river valley.

places.name: Goa Raja Waterfall
places.blurb: The King Cave waterfall: water spills through a cave-like rock opening.

places.name: Taxi and ferry to Nusa Penida
places.blurb: Car to Sanur harbour, then the fast boat across to Nusa Penida.

places.name: Padang Padang Inn
places.blurb: Simple bungalows a short walk from Padang Padang beach.

itineraries.title: One week in Bali
itineraries.summary: Start slow at a Nusa Dua resort, day-trip to Nusa Penida, base in Ubud for temples and a Mount Batur sunrise hike, finish with Tanah Lot and Canggu beach clubs.
itineraries.creator: racheloffduty

items.name: SafetyWing Travel Insurance
items.note: Essential for emergency medical coverage, trip protection, and optional adventure sports coverage in Bali.
items.priceNote: Essential plan, ages 18-39, $62.72 per 4 weeks (creator: a couple bucks a day)

items.name: Marriott's Bali Nusa Dua Gardens
items.note: Great for a relaxing first day to beat jet-lag with a resort feel and dedicated beach shuttles.
items.priceNote: per night, 1-bedroom (date-dependent) (creator: bookable with Marriott points)

items.name: Nusa Dua Beach
items.note: Guaranteed beach time with reserved hotel cabanas or space on the sand for non-guests.

items.name: Bali Collection
items.note: The main spot in the area for grabbing some shopping.

items.name: Uluwatu Temple
items.note: Built on the edge of a cliff, it provides an amazing vantage point of South Bali's epic cliffs and pristine beaches.

items.name: Kecak Dance Performance
items.note: A rhythmic musical and choreographed skit performance at sunset; well worth seeing for first-timers.

items.name: Bumbu Bali
items.note: A sizable restaurant serving exclusively Balinese cuisine.
items.priceNote: rijsttafel set menu, price on site

items.name: Ferry from Sanur to Nusa Penida
items.note: A 40-minute ferry ride; wear clothes above the knees as you have to wade shin-deep in water to board.

items.name: West Nusa Penida (Kelingking Beach, Angel's Billabong, Broken Beach, Crystal Bay)
items.note: Stunning, unbelievable beaches that make the trek to the island completely worth it.
items.priceNote: shared day tour incl. boat & lunch

items.name: Diamond Beach
items.note: An epic must-visit beach on the eastern side of the island.

items.name: Maruti Beach Club
items.note: Convenient spot near the dock to relax by the pool; the smoothies are great though the food is average.
items.priceNote: sunbed minimum spend (creator: free to use facilities with food/drink purchase)

items.name: Sanur to Ubud Drive
items.note: Takes 1-2 hours depending on traffic; highly recommend arranging a private driver ahead of time.

items.name: Ubud Art Market
items.note: Wander around and pick up beautiful woven bags, scarves, or jewelry.

items.name: Mount Batur Sunrise Hike
items.note: Requires a 2 AM wake-up call, but the 1.5-2 hour guided hike yields incredible sunrise views from the volcano.

items.name: Tegalalang Rice Terraces
items.note: Make this your first stop to beat the crowds and enjoy the beautiful morning light.

items.name: Goa Gajah & Pura Gunung Lebah
items.note: Beautiful nearby temples; Goa Gajah has a carved demon entrance, and Gunung Lebah is the birthplace of Ubud.

items.name: Copper Kitchen and Bar
items.note: A fun rooftop spot perfect for a fancier night out.

items.name: Alchemy
items.note: Alchemy for raw/vegan.

items.name: Umah Pizza
items.note: Umah for cozy pizza.

items.name: Warung Di Koi
items.note: Warung Di Koi for solid mie goreng.

items.name: No Más
items.note: Vibrant nightlife spots for grabbing drinks, dancing to live music, and mingling.

items.name: Radiantly Alive
items.note: Take a class in open-air studios with natural lighting and views of rice terraces.

items.name: Pura Tanah Lot
items.note: Very crowded but an absolutely iconic and breathtaking spot to catch the sunset.

items.name: Canggu Beach Clubs (The Lawn, Finns, La Brisa)
items.note: Choose your vibe from open-air casual, lively poolside DJs, or reclaimed wood Mediterranean atmospheres.
items.priceNote: free entry; daybeds have min spend

items.name: The Shady Shack
items.note: A breezy, vegetarian health food cafe overlooking the rice fields.

itineraries.title: 10 days of luxury Bali
itineraries.summary: Seminyak spas and fine dining, Uluwatu cliff pools and beach clubs, Ubud culture and rice terraces, East Bali water palaces, and a Nusa Penida day trip.
itineraries.creator: vamosbitchachos

items.name: Coffee Cartel
items.note: A little coffee shop with the freshest produce and the tastiest breakfast options.

items.name: Prana Spa
items.note: A perfect place to kick back, relax, and enjoy a spa treatment.

items.name: W Hotel
items.note: Great beachfront spot with endless pools and an energetic atmosphere.

items.name: Merah Putih
items.note: Authentic Balinese fine dining with 10/10 lobster dumplings; book in advance.
items.priceNote: 10-dish tasting menu per person (creator: relatively pricey)

items.name: The Edge
items.note: Ultimate #poolgoals; make sure to reserve a table early to secure your spot.
items.priceNote: day pass incl. IDR 600k F&B credit

items.name: Green Bowl Beach
items.note: A gorgeous, secluded beach perfect for exploring.

items.name: Sundays Beach Club
items.note: An amazing beach club setting with great vibes.
items.priceNote: day pass incl. F&B credit & cable car

items.name: Sarong
items.note: Another fantastic dinner option known for excellent service and tasting menus.

items.name: Ubud Shopping
items.note: Pick up souvenirs like the popular twine bags and local household products.

items.name: Royal Ubud Palace Fire Show
items.note: A cultural evening show starting around 8:30 PM; arrive early for good seats.

items.name: Tegallalang Rice Terrace
items.note: Incredibly famous, vast rice terraces with spectacular, dream-like views.

items.name: Tirta Gangga Water Palace
items.note: Former royal home featuring beautiful carved statues, lush gardens, and iconic koi fish ponds.

items.name: Gates of Heaven (Lempuyang Temple)
items.note: Felt like a social media trap with nothing to see but two gates; not worth the hype.

items.name: Kelingking Beach
items.note: Breathtaking T-Rex shaped viewpoint; arrive early so you have energy to hike down and back up.

items.name: Crystal Bay Beach
items.note: Crystal clear water making it ideal for snorkeling, diving, or just kicking back for a tan.

items.name: Ubud Rafting
items.note: Highly rated by others as a trip highlight, though the creator skipped it due to personal preference.

items.name: Tegenungan Waterfall
items.note: A stunning, accessible waterfall located in the southern part of Bali.

items.name: Tirta Empul Temple
items.note: The creator's biggest regret to miss; watch thousands bathe in thousand-year-old curative holy springs.

itineraries.title: 3-week Bali road trip
itineraries.summary: A slow loop of the whole island by car: Denpasar and the Bukit beaches, Seminyak and Canggu, the rice terraces and lakes of the centre, Ubud, Mount Batur, Sidemen, Amed's reefs, Lovina's dolphins and the wild west.
itineraries.creator: globalviewpoint

items.name: Bajra Sandhi Monument
items.note: Start in Denpasar with Bali's independence monument and museum.

items.name: Pasar Badung
items.note: Denpasar's big local market.

items.name: Warung Blanjong
items.note: Nasi campur in Sanur.
items.priceNote: about IDR 145k per person with drinks

items.name: Sanur Beach
items.note: Walk the beachfront path.

items.name: Puri Santrian
items.note: Or The Bene Hotel.

items.name: Uluwatu Temple
items.note: Clifftop temple; stay for sunset.

itineraries.title: Bali on a backpacker budget
itineraries.summary: Two packed days based out of Ubud and Canggu on about $30 a day: terraces, temples and waterfalls, then surf, beach clubs and the Uluwatu fire dance, with optional extras for a third day.
itineraries.creator: thebrokebackpacker

items.name: Kampung Cafe
items.note: Lunch with a terrace view.

items.name: Layana Warung
items.note: Vegetarian-friendly.

items.name: Saraswati Temple
items.note: On Jalan Raya Ubud with Ubud Palace and the Blanco museum.

items.name: Ubud Palace
items.note: Nightly dance shows.

items.name: Prasaja by Arang
items.note: Dinner, then Tukies Coconut Shop for dessert.

items.name: Campuhan Ridge Walk
items.note: About 2 hours. Start 6:00-7:30 am to beat the heat.

items.name: Bali Swing
items.note: Lunch at The Plantation Restaurant nearby.

items.name: Ubud Art Market
items.note: Haggle: it's customary. Bintang at OOPS next door.

items.name: Potato Head Beach Club
items.note: About an hour's drive from Ubud to Seminyak.
items.priceNote: IDR 250k entry 4:30-7pm, credited to F&B; free earlier

items.name: Surf lesson in Canggu
items.note: Experienced surfers can rent a board at SandBar for about $4 (2 hours).

items.name: Waterbom Bali
items.note: Cashless wristband inside. Eat at The Shack or Thaitalian.

items.name: Suluban Beach
items.note: Experienced surfers only. Cold Bintang from the stalls at the bottom.

items.name: Uluwatu Temple
items.note: Monkeys steal things; you can usually trade them back for fruit.

items.name: Kecak Dance Performance
items.note: 6 pm fire dance.

items.name: Warung Bejana
items.note: About 400 m from the temple.

items.name: Tribal Bali
items.note: Co-working hostel with a pool.
items.priceNote: per night, dorm bed; privates from $50

items.name: Pura Besakih
items.note: Creator: go with a guide (about $70 tour with pickup) to avoid scammers.
items.priceNote: IDR 150k incl. sarong, guide, shuttle (creator: about $1)

items.name: Mount Batur Sunrise Hike
items.note: Pickup around 2 am.

items.name: Tanah Lot
items.note: Not reachable at high tide: check the tides.

items.name: La Plancha
items.note: Sunset drinks on the beanbags.

itineraries.title: 7 days in Bali
itineraries.summary: The classic first-timer week: beach clubs in Canggu, three nights in Ubud, a Mount Batur sunrise, a Nusa Penida day trip and the Kecak dance in Uluwatu.
itineraries.creator: saltinourhair

items.name: Amar Boutique Hotel
items.note: Or Cali Villas, Guru Canggu; in Seminyak The Legian, Elysian, Villa Air.

items.name: Canggu beach clubs (La Brisa, The Lawn)
items.note: Or Potato Head and Mari Beach Club in Seminyak, 20 minutes away.
items.priceNote: free entry; daybeds have min spend

items.name: Taxi to Ubud
items.note: Grab or GoJek is slightly cheaper.

items.name: The Kayon Jungle Resort
